races.name: Racing Foundation Supports The NHC EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Or Another
runners_data.comment: January foal by Dark Angel; 180,000gns yearling; family of 2yo winners; respected on debut
runners_data.spotlight: January foal by Dark Angel; 180,000gns yearling; first foal; dam unraced half-sister to winners Tactical (6f 2yo Group 2), Handcuffed (6f 2yo) and Works Of Art (Listed-placed 6f 2yo), out of Listed-placed 6f 2yo winner, is granddaughter to 7f 2yo Group 3 winner; that pedigree suggests he'll make his mark as a juvenile; much respected on this introduction for powerful yard.

runners_data.name: Spectacular Diver
runners_data.comment: April foal by Dandy Man; £10,000 yearling; speedy pedigree for last year's winning yard
runners_data.spotlight: April foal by Dandy Man; £10,000 yearling; third foal; half-brother to 5f winner Military Girl (including 2yo; RPR 78); dam 5.7f/6f winner (93), closely related to AW sprint winners Tilly Trotter and Dee Sprinter, out of useful 5f 2yo winning half-sister to 5f 2yo Group 2 winner Green Door; speedy pedigree and yard won this last year with a subsequent Listed-winning filly, albeit she'd already had a run; betting should be informative ahead of this debut.

runners_data.name: Black Cuillin
runners_data.comment: April foal by Far Above; dam 7f/1m winner; family of Irish Leger winner; market can guide
runners_data.spotlight: April foal by Far Above; fourth foal; dam 7f/1m winner (RPR 83), closely related to 1m winner Kelowna, out of 7.5f-8.5f Listed winning half-sister to Irish St Leger winner Sans Frontieres; quite encouraging she's hitting the track this early, albeit might be one for further down the line; market can guide.

runners_data.name: Innichen
runners_data.comment: Excuses on debut and stepped up when second last time; can put experience to good use
runners_data.spotlight: Early February foal by Mehmas; £65,000 yearling; excuses when promising sixth at Bath on debut this month and stepped up when second at Newmarket (also 5f, good) a fortnight ago; the only one of these with experience and there should be better to come.

races.name: Sir Peter O'Sullevan Charitable Trust Supports NHC EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Night Wolf
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from a 184-day break but showed clear ability in that York maiden and should appreciate this easier company.
runners_data.comment: Promising debut at York (7f, good to firm) before a lesser run on good to soft; unexposed
runners_data.spotlight: Promising debut in a traditionally strong York maiden last August (7f, good to firm; trained by John and Sean Quinn); couldn't build on it on a slower surface at Redcar in October (stable debut); remains with potential and this trip should suit on pedigree.

runners_data.name: Why Not Win
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity with top jockey booked, but the 184-day absence and lack of recent form data makes him hard to assess.

runners_data.name: Infraad
runners_data.note: Raced too freely at Nottingham last time but Haggas runners often improve for their reappearance and he has solid form figures.
runners_data.comment: Two promising placed efforts 166 days apart; can do better still; leading form claims
runners_data.spotlight: Promising 2yo debut (1m, soft); beaten as a strong favourite at Nottingham on his reappearance (1m2f, good) three weeks ago, racing too freely; remains capable of better and he is a leading form contender.

runners_data.name: Asia Force
runners_data.note: Natural leader with recent race fitness advantage, but his AW form needs to translate to turf under what could be his first real pressure.
runners_data.comment: Promise in two AW runs this winter (1m2f-1m3f); open to improvement but probably needs it
runners_data.spotlight: Clear promise in two AW novice events over the winter (1m2f/1m3f, Tapeta); can do better but likely he will need to if he is to make a winning turf debut.

runners_data.name: Sea Lantern
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 240-day break who showed stamina at longer trips but needs everything to fall right from the rear.
runners_data.comment: 1m4f soft-ground win in Ireland when last seen; sold 75,000gns since; tough task today
runners_data.spotlight: Ran twice over 1m4f at Roscommon for Jack Davison last summer, finishing third on debut (good) before seeing off 14 rivals on soft ground a fortnight later; can win more races for new connections (sold for 75,000gns last October) but he drops in trip on faster ground and has to concede chunks of weight to some promising 3yos so this might not be one of them.

runners_data.name: Leighton
runners_data.note: Bred for much better but disappointed on debut and faces a fitness test after 177 days off the track.
runners_data.comment: Top-class pedigree; should leave his 2yo effort (1m) well behind him over middle distances
runners_data.spotlight: Top-class middle-distance pedigree, by Frankel out of a Group 1 winner in these colours; 2-1 joint-favourite for his Kempton debut in November (1m) but ran green and couldn't threaten in a race won by a smart prospect; should be a different proposition this year now his stamina is being drawn out.

races.paceDynamic: Asia Force will lead from the gates with no obvious pace rival, setting a comfortable tempo over this extended trip. Night Wolf and Infraad will sit handy in the prominent positions, with Why Not Win's positioning uncertain as a newcomer. The back-runners Sea Lantern and Leighton will need the pace to collapse in the final stages to be competitive from their hold-up positions. This sustainable pace scenario strongly favours the prominent runners who can track the leader and pounce when Asia Force's stamina is tested.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Asia Force sets manageable fractions and the prominent horses get first run
scenarios.body: Night Wolf and Infraad can utilise their higher ratings by stalking the leader and kicking clear when Asia Force weakens. The hold-up horses will struggle to make up ground from the back of this small field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Asia Force's winter form translates to turf and he maintains his gallop
scenarios.body: The Burke-trained leader uses his recent race fitness to see off the challengers who haven't raced for months. His stamina-laden breeding should help him stay this extended distance under pressure.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves too strong and the front-runners tire badly
scenarios.body: Sea Lantern's proven stamina at longer trips allows him to pick up the pieces from the back, with Leighton's class pedigree finally showing. The prominent runners pay for racing too close to unsustainable fractions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Newcomer Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Why Not Win shows significant improvement from his juveniles days
scenarios.body: McDonald rides a patient race on the Johnston newcomer who has been gelded and steps up in trip. The lack of early pace allows him to settle and his unexposed profile gives him an edge over these exposed rivals.

watchPoints.text: Asia Force breaking too fast from the front as Burke horses can sometimes do, setting up the race for the closers
Infraad settling properly for Marquand after racing too keenly at Nottingham which cost him the race
Why Not Win's early positioning with McDonald as it will reveal Johnston's tactics and the horse's wellbeing
Night Wolf's jumping from the gates after such a long break, as any slow start would be costly in this small field
Sea Lantern needing a strong pace to aim at from the rear, as any crawl will make his task impossible

races.name: NARS Supports The National Horseracing College Handicap

runners_data.name: Keldeo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with C&D form who won well at Catterick from a wide stall, suggesting the draw won't hinder him significantly here
runners_data.comment: C&D winner last April; arrives on the back of a 6f Catterick win; widest stall not ideal
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner 12 months ago (good ground); back to winning ways in a 6f handicap at Catterick three weeks ago, doing well from a wide stall; has landed the widest draw again today and that could find her out.

runners_data.name: Alpine Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs the pace to collapse but has strong turf form on good ground with five career wins to her name
runners_data.comment: Return to turf in her favour and this mark is in range; one to be interested in
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time turf winner; only 2lb higher than for her Redcar win last summer (6f, good to firm) and her two AW runs this year aren't the ones to judge her on (blindfold slow to be removed last time); leading contender.

runners_data.name: General Assembly
runners_data.note: Front-running type returning from 62-day break with solid AW form but faces a challenging wide draw that may compromise his tactics
runners_data.comment: In good form on AW when last seen; not much wiggle room off current mark though
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; two AW wins (5f) last autumn and he was in good form when last seen in February; not much wiggle room off this mark though and a lower draw would have been preferable too.

runners_data.name: Call To Action
runners_data.note: Natural leader returning from 296-day layoff but showed his best form in blinkers last summer and gets that key headgear again
runners_data.comment: Revived by blinkers last summer, winning cosily at Ripon 296 days ago; revised mark fair
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 5yo; revived by blinkers last summer, following his Redcar fourth with a cosy win at Ripon (5f, good) 296 days ago; this 3lb higher mark is unlikely to prove beyond him but he is taking on match-fit opposition today.

runners_data.name: Jojo Rabbit
runners_data.note: Made all winner over C&D who drops back from 6f where he disappointed, with low draw offering tactical advantage in a wide-drawn field
runners_data.comment: Made all for C&D win 3 weeks ago; below best on AW (6f) latest; can bounce back quickly
runners_data.spotlight: Made all to win over C&D on his penultimate start (good to soft; Class 6); not in the same form over 6f on AW 12 days ago but he is well drawn back at 5f and his rider's 3lb claim is a bonus; key player.

runners_data.name: Toomuchforme
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing tongue tie and visor but hard to trust after his Southwell surprise was followed by two poor efforts
runners_data.comment: 33-1 win at Southwell (5f) last month has been followed by two modest runs; opposable
runners_data.spotlight: Sprung a 33-1 surprise at Southwell last month (5f) but that has been followed by two disappointing runs; best turf form on good ground; others appeal more for win purposes.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer moving up 4lb after Newcastle AW win but needs strong pace to be effective over this minimum trip
runners_data.comment: 5f AW win 16 days ago was a good effort; 4lb higher mark demands extra from him
runners_data.spotlight: Stepped up on his low-key reappearance when winning a 5f handicap at Newcastle 16 days ago; this demands more up 4lb and he wasn't at his best in one C&D run last summer.

runners_data.name: Invincible Crown
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 142-day break who seems better suited to AW surfaces based on recent evidence
runners_data.comment: Perhaps better on AW than turf; trainer also runs Jojo Rabbit who makes more appeal
runners_data.spotlight: Seems happiest on AW nowadays; not at best at Wolverhampton when last seen in December; trainer may have stronger claims with Jojo Rabbit.

races.paceDynamic: Call To Action will look to lead from his wide draw, with General Assembly and Jojo Rabbit likely to press the early pace from better positions. The presence of multiple prominent runners should create a solid gallop over this minimum trip, though nothing suggests it will be overly fierce. Alpine Girl and Rock Of England will need the pace to collapse to be effective from their hold-up positions. This race shape clearly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and strike in the final furlong, as they'll benefit from the honest gallop without being caught up in early scrimmaging.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but sustainable with Call To Action leading
scenarios.body: The prominent trio of Keldeo, General Assembly and Jojo Rabbit get ideal positions to strike, while the hold-up horses find insufficient pace collapse to close the gap effectively.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Call To Action goes too fast early or the prominent runners engage too soon
scenarios.body: The strong pace sets up perfectly for Alpine Girl and Rock Of England to close from the rear with their superior finishing kicks. Hold-up horses finally get the race shape they need over this sharp 5f trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Call To Action gets an uncontested lead and the prominent runners fail to apply pressure
scenarios.body: The Easterby runner gets first run from the front and holds on grimly, with the prominent runners struggling to close the gap in time. His 296-day break becomes irrelevant if he controls the pace from flag to finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Turns Messy
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses want the lead early and create a scrambling pace from the wide draws
scenarios.body: The uneven tempo suits whoever can find clear running at the right moment, likely favouring the most experienced campaigners. Jockey tactics become crucial when positions get compromised by the wide stall numbers.

watchPoints.text: Call To Action's fitness after 296 days off could see him weaken quickly if he sets too strong a pace from his wide draw
Alpine Girl and Rock Of England need the pace to develop strongly early or they'll have too much ground to make up over 5f
General Assembly's wide draw may force him into an attacking ride that doesn't suit his stamina-laden profile over this minimum trip
Jojo Rabbit's low draw gives him a significant tactical advantage in a field where most runners face wide stalls
The good ground conditions clearly favour Keldeo and Alpine Girl based on their recent form patterns and historical preferences

races.name: Tuffa Boots Supports The National Horseracing College Handicap

runners_data.name: Billyb
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent recent record returning after 159 days, but two 1m wins in 2025 suggest this trip suits perfectly
runners_data.comment: As good as ever last year, winning twice, but returns from an absence minus cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Added another two 1m wins to his CV in 2025, including on AW when last seen in November; this 2lb higher mark shouldn't prove beyond him but his record fresh, allied to the absence of cheekpieces (worn on last seven starts), suggest this may not be his day.

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: Lone front runner will get his own way early but veteran legs may not withstand sustained pressure from 2f out
runners_data.comment: Conditions won't faze him and on a dangerous mark; needs to leave recent return behind him
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran with 14 wins to his name, two of them coming over C&D; ended 2025 quietly and he finished behind a couple of today's rivals at Ripon on his reappearance 13 days ago; on a dangerous mark but he may need another run before he is of major interest.

runners_data.name: Sailthisshipalone
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with winning form over course and distance but needs to avoid the inevitable traffic problems
runners_data.comment: C&D win on stable debut this month; up 3lb in a higher grade and with cheekpieces absent
runners_data.spotlight: Soft-ground win for Richard Fahey last November (1m); tongue tied for the first time when making a winning stable debut over C&D three weeks ago (good to soft); 3lb higher in a better race and going without cheekpieces today; handles good ground but perhaps wouldn't want it any faster.

runners_data.name: Walsingham
runners_data.note: Classy prominent runner who completed hat-trick over course and distance, returned with promising third at Ripon 13 days ago
runners_data.comment: C&D record of 311; encouraging reappearance at Ripon; untried on ground faster than good
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a hat-trick last summer with the first two legs coming over C&D (good ground); promising third at Ripon on his seasonal return two weeks ago, keeping on well from 2f out having earlier clipped a rival's heels as the race was hotting up; still has more to offer and the drying ground is the only imponderable (unraced on faster than good).

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 208 days but back to last winning mark and has strong course record
runners_data.comment: Three wins last summer at around 1m; on last winning mark but has 208-day absence to defy
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins last May/July at about 1m on various ground and he's back down to his last winning mark; ended 2025 quietly and there's a suspicion he'll improve for this comeback run; withdrawn after getting upset in the stalls at Ripon two weeks ago (25-1 at the time).

runners_data.name: Leadenhall
runners_data.note: Last year's winner of this race and hold-up style perfectly suited, but 184 days off track raises fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Won this race after a break last year; on a good mark and more appealing than many
runners_data.spotlight: Ran out the easy winner of the corresponding event (good ground) on his reappearance last April; also successful at Haydock in August and that win came off a 2lb higher mark; interesting on return from a six-month break.

runners_data.name: On The River
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid form but needs to secure early position among the congested pack
runners_data.comment: Two solid runs this year and fully effective over C&D; drying ground the concern this time
runners_data.spotlight: Won last summer's Carlisle Bell off this mark (1m, soft); ran well when fifth in the Spring Mile at Doncaster on his return before finding only his stablemate Milteye too strong at Ripon 13 days ago (1m, good to soft; Walsingham back in third); fully effective over C&D but he appears to have a preference for slower than good now and drying conditions aren't sure to suit.

runners_data.name: Sir Paul Ramsey
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with good ground form but 4-year-old may lack tactical experience in this competitive field
runners_data.comment: Dangerous on best form but has to rebound from a lacklustre run at Musselburgh 17 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Two turf wins at around 1m on good ground last summer, the second of them coming off a 1lb higher mark; not far off his best form when fourth at Lingfield early this month but he has since finished a remote 11th at Musselburgh; not a solid option.

runners_data.name: Vincent Rocks
runners_data.note: Prominent runner stepping up to handicaps after winning novice races but question marks over this step up in class
runners_data.comment: 2-2 in novice company but both handicap runs have resulted in heavy defeats; headgear now
runners_data.spotlight: Won novice races at Nottingham (8.3f, good to soft) and Southwell (1m, AW) on his first two starts; flopped on handicap debut last September (1m2f, good to soft) and he was out the back in the Spring Mile on his reappearance 32 days ago; down in class but he needs the cheekpieces/faster ground to turn things around.

races.paceDynamic: Garden Oasis is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate a sustainable gallop from flag to finish without early pressure. The real battle develops behind him where Sailthisshipalone, Walsingham, On The River, Sir Paul Ramsey and Vincent Rocks all want prominent positions, creating a dangerous traffic jam approaching the final 2-3 furlongs. With 5 of 9 runners wanting to be handy, the pace will quicken sharply when they fan out for racing room, stretching the field significantly. This congested prominent group and inevitable acceleration strongly favours the hold-up horses who can avoid the early scrimmaging and finish through tired legs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates the expected traffic problems and pace acceleration
scenarios.body: The 5-horse scrum behind Garden Oasis will create stop-start running and a strong gallop from 3f out, perfectly suiting patient tactics. Billyb, Cosmos Raj and Leadenhall can all pick their way through and finish strongest when others have used their energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivors Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If one or two from the prominent group can secure a clean run without getting trapped
scenarios.body: Sailthisshipalone and Walsingham have the class to navigate the traffic and maintain their position when the pace lifts. Their recent form suggests they can handle both the tactical pressure and finish strongly when others fade around them.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Garden Oasis Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the lone leader gets an easy time in front and the prominent pack neutralises each other
scenarios.body: Garden Oasis will get soft sectionals early with no pressure, then hold off a divided finish as the pack behind sorts itself out too late. His course and distance record gives him every chance if the pace scenario falls his way perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Oasis sets a pedestrian gallop and the prominent group settles behind him
scenarios.body: A dawdling pace will set up a cavalry charge finish where any horse can win in a blanket finish. The lack of early pace pressure means stamina becomes less important and it becomes a pure speed test over the final 2f.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems 3f out when Sailthisshipalone, Walsingham, On The River, Sir Paul Ramsey and Vincent Rocks all need racing room simultaneously
Garden Oasis could get an uncontested lead but watch for his stamina reserves in final furlong at age 11
Billyb and Cosmos Raj both return from long breaks so watch for fitness/sharpness in market moves
Watch early positioning of Leadenhall who won this race last year but may need the run after 184-day absence
Daniel Tudhope on Walsingham has strong partnership with David O'Meara stable and knows horse's tactical needs well

races.name: HBLB Supports The National Horseracing College Handicap

runners_data.name: Sixtygeesbaby
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose ability to pressure Veblen Good early will determine the race dynamics and his own chances.
runners_data.comment: Not fired on good to soft for new yard; faster ground can help and he is well treated now
runners_data.spotlight: Not at his best in two runs for David O'Meara but on good to soft ground; possible this return to a faster surface will help and he's undoubtedly well handicapped if it does; waters muddied slightly by the stable also having Veblen Good in the race.

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: Front runner returning from 236-day break who should control the pace uncontested given the field composition.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed in sprint handicaps; drops in class for stable debut; interesting contender
runners_data.spotlight: AW winner (5f) for Karl Burke as a 2yo; ran well over C&D on last season's reappearance and his fourth in a big field at York on his handicap debut came off a 3lb higher mark; two subsequent efforts are excusable (Listed company and then 7f on slow ground); sold for 32,000gns in October; unexposed as a sprinter and now drops in class; stable also runs Sixtygeesbaby.

runners_data.name: The Good Biscuit
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with excellent course record who needs the pace to collapse to be effective from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Two course wins last year; promising return at Catterick; firmly in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: Two course wins last year, over 6f on good ground in July and 5f on soft in October; pleasing third at Catterick on his reappearance three weeks ago; should go well with Warren Fentiman taking off a useful 3lb.

runners_data.name: Modern Times
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner in good current form whose recent Ripon run suggests he's ready to strike after his long absence.
runners_data.comment: Shaped nicely at Ripon on his return two weeks ago; leading claims if building on it
runners_data.spotlight: Ripon maiden win (6f, good) last June on his second start for Tim Easterby; shaped nicely on his return from ten months off back at Ripon two weeks ago, poorly positioned but running the fastest final 2f split to snatch a never-dangerous fifth; should be sharper today and he's interesting off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Mystical Storm
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 186 days following wind surgery, relying on pace collapse and latent ability.
runners_data.comment: 6f novice win last summer; ended 2025 quietly and others are preferred this time
runners_data.spotlight: Underwent wind surgery prior to his Doncaster novice success last July (6f, good); ran well in a 7f handicap at York two weeks later but his form dropped off afterwards; gelded during his absence; dangerous mark but may find others having his measure now back from a break.

runners_data.name: Alpha Magic
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner fresh after 282 days who has shown course form but faces a significant fitness test.
runners_data.comment: Disappointing when last seen but he'd looked promising beforehand; best days still to come
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointed at Ayr when last seen 282 days ago; he had looked promising beforehand though and still has potential; can go well fresh but he is held by Sixtygeesbaby on their Doncaster run 12 months ago.

races.paceDynamic: Veblen Good is the only confirmed front runner and will set his own tempo from the start without pressure. With four of six runners showing hold-up tendencies (The Good Biscuit, Modern Times, Mystical Storm, Alpha Magic) and only Sixtygeesbaby likely to race prominently, this creates a scenario where the pace-setter controls proceedings. The lack of early pace pressure means Veblen Good can dictate fractions while the hold-up brigade waits behind, potentially leaving themselves with too much to do in the final stages. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can sit close to the uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Veblen Good Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If Veblen Good jumps well and faces no early pressure from Sixtygeesbaby
scenarios.body: He dictates comfortable fractions throughout and the hold-up horses find themselves chasing shadows when the pace quickens. The prominent racers benefit from tracking the uncontested leader while back markers struggle to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sixtygeesbaby Applies Early Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Sixtygeesbaby breaks sharply and forces Veblen Good into a pace duel
scenarios.body: The two prominent runners soften each other up through honest fractions, setting up the race for one of the stronger hold-up horses to strike late. Modern Times or The Good Biscuit can capitalise on their tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mystical Storm Fresh Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the returning Mystical Storm benefits from his wind surgery and 186-day break
scenarios.body: His hold-up style works perfectly as the front runners collapse after going too hard early, and his previous course form gives him the edge in the finish. The long break proves beneficial rather than detrimental.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Alpha Magic Breaks Absence
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha Magic's 282-day absence doesn't blunt his ability to finish strongly
scenarios.body: His hold-up running style proves perfectly suited as the pace collapses in front of him, and his previous course success translates into a bold fresh performance. The Easterby team's patient approach with him pays dividends.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Sixtygeesbaby breaks slowly as this hands Veblen Good an unassailable tactical advantage from the front
Monitor Veblen Good's jumping from the stalls after his long break as any tardiness ruins his front-running tactics
Observe Modern Times early positioning as any attempt to race more prominently than usual signals confidence
Watch for market support for the two long-absent horses Mystical Storm and Alpha Magic as it may indicate hidden fitness
Check if The Good Biscuit gets squeezed for racing room in the final furlong given his hold-up running style

races.name: Chadwick Lawrence Supports National Horseracing College Handicap

runners_data.name: Piecederesistance
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 270 days off with new headgear, likely to get an uncontested lead but stamina questions after long break
runners_data.comment: 2022 C&D win but was running poorly over hurdles when last seen; tongue-tie for yard debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won in France in 2020 and scored over C&D in 2022 but has developed a rocky profile and was in poor form when last seen over hurdles in the autumn; has joined Martin Keighley (same owners) but watching brief advised on this comeback in a tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Bearwith
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer but can race closer than most, strong course record and was second in this race last year with solid recent form
runners_data.comment: Fine effort from wide stall when second (1m2f, good) last time; has form here; big player
runners_data.spotlight: Second in the 2024 running of this; nine wins include five on turf, all around this trip on a sound surface; won at Newcastle (AW) in February and it was a fine effort from the widest stall when second of 14 at Nottingham (also 1m2f, good) 11 days ago; big shout.

runners_data.name: Lightening Company
runners_data.note: Pure hold-up horse who needs strong pace, claiming jockey aboard but has winning course form and ran well here last time
runners_data.comment: All of nothing of late but scored over 1m4f here latest; key player if ground is okay
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time Flat winner, including C&D, who has been all or nothing since scoring over hurdles at Cartmel in July; three AW no-shows followed good second over C&D (soft; 40-1) in October but market support predicted a going day when scoring here (1m4f, good to soft) three weeks ago; might not want the ground to get too quick but otherwise a key player under 2lb nudge.

runners_data.name: Finlaggan
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with concerning finishing record, minimal experience on good ground but decent breeding suggests better possible
runners_data.comment: Uncompetitive in two maidens for this yard; market check essential for handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Midfield on sole start for Andre Fabre last April; not competitive in a maiden on AW and turf (1m/7f) this spring but bred to be much better than he's shown so far; market watch essential on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Dubawi Time
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 205 days off with new headgear, has won twice this year but long absence is worry
runners_data.comment: 0-8 last year but starts out for new yard from career-low mark; worthy of a market check
runners_data.spotlight: 1m4f AW handicap win for the Gosdens and doubled his tally in soft-ground handicap at Yarmouth (1m2f) for William Knight, both in 2024; couldn't recapture that form last year and was sold for 8,000gns in October; starts out for new yard from career-low mark so worth a check of the betting.

runners_data.name: Heartened
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with just one win from 17 starts, acts on this trip but inconsistent profile makes her hard to trust
runners_data.comment: Trip an excuse last time but she's out of the handicap and has work to do
runners_data.spotlight: One win from 17 attempts came over 1m2f (AW; acts on sound turf) in September; reappearance fourth in AW classified wasn't a bad effort in March and she likely didn't stay 1m4f last time; still has work to do from out of the handicap back on grass.

races.paceDynamic: Piecederesistance will likely lead from the start with minimal early pressure, as most runners (Bearwith, Lightening Company, Finlaggan, Heartened) prefer to settle off the pace. Dubawi Time may sit prominent but the overall tempo should be steady rather than fierce early on. The lack of natural pace-pressers means Piecederesistance can dictate comfortable fractions before the hold-up horses launch their challenges in the straight. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those who can travel well in the first half of the field, as they'll avoid traffic problems that could hamper the many hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Piecederesistance gets an easy lead and maintains galloping room turning for home.
scenarios.body: The pace-setter can control the race from pillar to post while the hold-up brigade gets in each other's way behind. Bearwith's prominent style gives him the best chance to track and challenge the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely slow and bunches the field for a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: The superior class horses get their preferred strong gallop from the back and have clear runs to overwhelm tired leaders. Lightening Company and Bearwith have the tactical speed to capitalize on a messy finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses get stopped for runs while prominent runners stay clear.
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace leads to a wall of horses turning in, creating interference for many while those racing handier avoid trouble. Dubawi Time's prominent position and Bearwith's class help them navigate best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Piecederesistance stops quickly after setting slow fractions and Dubawi Time also fades.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery between the hold-up horses who must produce their best turns of foot from unpromising positions. Heartened's recent run and Finlaggan's breeding could see them emerge from the pack.

watchPoints.text: Piecederesistance could get an uncontested lead and prove hard to peg back if retaining any ability after the long break
Traffic problems are likely in the straight given five of six runners prefer to come from behind in a small field
Lightening Company needs others to go fast enough early to set up his finishing kick from the rear
Dubawi Time and Piecederesistance both return with headgear changes after lengthy absences which adds uncertainty
The claimer Harry Vigors takes a valuable 7lb off Lightening Company in what looks a competitive handicap

races.name: Yorkshire Society Supports The National Horseracing College Handicap

runners_data.name: Powerful Response
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid course form who benefits from this tactical setup and good recent Nottingham effort
runners_data.comment: Close third of 15 latest; well drawn again and he's respected; first-time visor
runners_data.spotlight: Two soft-ground turf wins, including one for this yard, but he acts on better ground and made the most of a good draw when close third of 15 at Nottingham (8.5f, good; Token Love seventh) in cheekpieces three weeks ago; that is just about the best recent form on offer and he's nicely berthed again; visor goes on and he's respected.

runners_data.name: Volenti
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 88-day break under inexperienced 7lb claimer, needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Struggled after close fourth over C&D (g/f) in August; reduced mark and back from a break
runners_data.spotlight: Last of his five wins came 15 months ago and he struggled after close fourth over C&D (good to firm) in August; falling mark a help if he can stage a revival after three-month break; market check advised.

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with course win and wind surgery behind him, perfectly positioned to exploit lack of pace pressure
runners_data.comment: Six wins include one here; has been building up in two starts this term; could be poised
runners_data.spotlight: Six turf wins include one here (1m2f, good to firm) in August; had wind surgery before a fair comeback at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) in March and built on that when fifth of 14 at Nottingham (1m2f, good) 11 days ago; drop back in trip no reason to rule him out and he's respected.

runners_data.name: We've Got This
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning from 222-day absence, needs genuine gallop but has consistent record when fit
runners_data.comment: 7f winner (stays 1m) who generally runs her race; player if tuned up for this comeback
runners_data.spotlight: One win (7f, good to firm) from 11 starts but can generally be relied upon to run her race and it was another solid effort when second at Ayr (1m, soft) in September; ground/trip fine and market may reveal whether she's tuned up for this reappearance; big player if so.

runners_data.name: How's The Guvnor
runners_data.note: Prominent type freshened up after poor last run, dual AW winner for yard with tactical speed
runners_data.comment: Won twice (AW) in January; may have been freshened up by a break; not discounted
runners_data.spotlight: Won on turf as a 2yo for Clive Cox; dual AW winner (1m/7f) for this yard in January but poor last time when the race reportedly came too soon; has been freshened up and might bounce back.

runners_data.name: Boubyan
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner racing freely in cheekpieces, made all last win but versatile tactically
runners_data.comment: Turf winner but quiet on last two starts; mark is fine and he drops in grade
runners_data.spotlight: Made all on good to firm at Newbury (1m; first-time cheekpieces, kept since) in July and doubled his tally when picking up AW handicap (1m2f) in March; raced freely when underwhelming on last two starts but drops in grade and has already dipped below his last winning mark.

runners_data.name: Al Baahy
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping back up from classified company, bottom weight but needs pace to aim at
runners_data.comment: Turf winner; two AW classified wins in January; handicaps have been a struggle since
runners_data.spotlight: Turf winner back in May 2023 who found classified company his thing when going back-to-back on AW (9.5f/1m2f) in January; forced out of that grade subsequently and has found handicaps a stretch on last three starts.

runners_data.name: Bun Bang Fai
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making stable debut with new headgear after 209-day break, question marks everywhere
runners_data.comment: 7-race maiden; 4,000gns buy in October; hood/tongue-tie on for stable debut/reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Wasn't placed in seven starts around this trip for Archie Watson, including one go on turf; sold for 4,000gns in October; hood/tongue-tie deployed for this stable debut/reappearance and she's worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Token Love
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with tongue-tie fitted, consistent placer but yet to win in 23 starts
runners_data.comment: Shaped nicely on his return when ultimately midfield; tricky draw but still of interest
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to score but he went close at Wolverhampton (9.5f, AW) in December and was only beaten 3l despite finishing in midfield at Nottingham (8.5f, good; Powerful Response third) on his return three weeks ago; shaped well that day (hit the front before fading) and he's a candidate to build on that despite being drawn widest.

runners_data.name: Rajawail
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare reapplying blinkers, 23-race maiden trying optimum trip but limited ability
runners_data.comment: 23-race maiden who would be a surprise winner
runners_data.spotlight: 23-race maiden who has been tried at all manner of different trips, including 1m6f last time; this is arguably her best one and the reapplied blinkers might be a positive but she'd still be a surprise winner.

races.paceDynamic: Star Start will set the pace from the gates with no other confirmed front runners to press him early. This creates a sustainable tempo through the opening stages, allowing him to dictate terms without excessive pressure. The lack of natural pace angles means the gallop could develop into a tactical affair where positioning becomes crucial in the straight. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can position close to Star Start, as hold-up horses will struggle if the pace becomes pedestrian.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Star Start gets an uncontested lead and the pace becomes steady
scenarios.body: The front end gets first run in the straight and those with tactical speed can capitalize on good positioning. Hold-up horses get caught flat-footed when the kick comes.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses push Star Start along and create a genuine pace
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop sets up perfectly for the hold-up brigade to unleash finishing kicks. We've Got This and Boubyan get the race run to suit their styles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys get too cute and the pace crawls before a mad dash
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery with positioning crucial and amateur riders potentially caught out. Experience and track craft become paramount in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Star Start gets soft fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: His recent Pontefract course win and lack of early pressure allows him to control from pillar to post. The chasing pack struggles to peg back his advantage.

watchPoints.text: Star Start could get dangerously soft fractions with no pace pressure and prove hard to catch
Volenti's 7lb claiming jockey Harry Vigors may struggle tactically if the race becomes messy
We've Got This returning from 222-day break faces fitness questions despite her consistent record
Bun Bang Fai making stable debut for new connections with hood and tongue-tie first time
Multiple horses including Powerful Response and Token Love met at Nottingham with similar form lines
